plan.thesis: Nothing in these five apps is typed as a status: every status, count, age and verdict is derived from a dated record read against one stated as-of date, and every gate refuses until the evidence, the date and the named person it asks for are on the record.

tiers.beginner: THE REGISTER AND THE CALENDAR: complianceStatus, documentControl, calendar. Graded: six day counts.
tiers.intermediate: THE PLAN, THE NONCONFORMANCE AND THE CHECKLIST: qualityAssurance, auditManagement. Graded: four percents and two NCR ages.
tiers.advanced: THE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM: isoCompliance and the finding rules auditManagement imports. Graded: two coverage counts and four day counts.

digest.note: No section is history. SECTION 23 states the owner decisions in force, the owner ambiguities still open, and the five rules ASC-0 put in the engine at this course's request, each in the present tense with a measured figure.

grading.grader: public.academy_submit_capstone reads expected, tol and the answer as numeric, so every graded field is an integer and statuses, verdicts and dates are taught and never graded. A date is graded as calendar.daysUntil from the as-of date.
grading.tolerance: 0.5 for all eighteen (lead ruling after ASC-0, the same as riskchange): half a unit of the zero decimals an integer prints at, which admits exactly one integer and passes gradeprecision.py 18 of 18. One derivation: TOLERANCE in compliance_capstone.mjs.
grading.collisionRule: No graded value within its tolerance of the absolute value of any number token the digest prints (the go-live rule), and no two graded values within the looser of their tolerances.

findings.R2: REPAIRED UPSTREAM IN ASC-0: every percent is floor((200n+d)/2d); 57 of 200 prints 29. oracle_check.py's exact-half guard is RETIRED.
findings.R3: REPAIRED UPSTREAM IN ASC-0: certificateExpiring is 0 <= days <= 90; day 0 reads 'expires today'.
findings.R4: REPAIRED UPSTREAM IN ASC-0: a filed One-off reads 'Filed <date>. A one-off obligation, nothing further is due.' The dump now throws if any reason prints a negative day count.
findings.R5: REPAIRED UPSTREAM IN ASC-0: sentences name the register's standard; canSetClauseStatus takes the standard as a 4th argument. The digest prints the refusal for ISO 14001, 9001, 45001 and none.
findings.localDateOf: ASC-0 also reads a created_at instant as its local date in ncrAgeDays. No teaching or capstone NCR lacks raised_date, so nothing moved; the digest prints no localDateOf example because its answer is zone-dependent by design.
findings.clock: No clock read without an override. Proven by the source-read clock guard, the fake-clock rebuild and the static unguarded-call check.

decisions: Every graded field is an integer at tolerance 0.5 (lead ruling), because the academy grader is numeric only; dates are graded as daysUntil from the as-of date and enums are never graded.

The as-of date is 2026-10-15, built at local midnight; the reproducibility gate adds America/Los_Angeles and Pacific/Pago_Pago (UTC-11) to the three required zones because only a zone west of Greenwich can see a UTC parse, and its negative control proves it.
Graded counts come from a forty-clause ISO 45001 register so they clear the go-live collision rule; small counts would collide with the day and month tokens every printed date carries.
Manifests carry the three panel ids exactly as FC6's scaffold writes them, so courseContent.test.js 'every panel referenced is registered' is red until the panel phase registers them.
Lesson placeholders are title-only H1 files, because the content lint fails a manifest lesson with no file; FC6 wrote none.
